title: Acting without clinging, and your own dharma

verses.tr: As the ignorant act with attachment to action, so should the wise act without attachment, seeking the welfare of the world.
verses.angle: The wise act without attachment for the world
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now turns from his own example to the duty of the wise. Listen for the rule he sets for how they should act.

body.text: As the ignorant act with attachment to action, so should the wise act without attachment, seeking the welfare of the world. The word asaktah, without attachment, is the key here. The wise must act with the same energy as the ignorant, but stripped of personal clinging. Krishna then warns the wise not to unsettle the minds of those still attached to action.

verses.sa: न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् । जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन् ॥
verses.tr: An awakened person should not unsettle the minds of those attached to action. Instead, acting skillfully, such a person should engage them in all work.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues his teaching on how a wise person should behave in society.

body.text: An awakened person should not unsettle the minds of those attached to action. Instead, acting skillfully, such a person should engage them in all work. An awakened person should leave others' faith in action intact and lead by working well. Krishna then explains that all actions are driven by the qualities of nature.

verses.sa: प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः । अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते ॥
verses.tr: All actions are carried out in every way by the qualities of nature. Deluded by ego, a person thinks, 'I am the doer.'
verses.angle: The ego claims I am the doer
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks what truly drives action, and points to the ego that claims ownership over work performed by nature.

body.text: All actions are carried out in every way by the qualities of nature. Deluded by ego, a person thinks, 'I am the doer.' The verse reveals a split between the doer and the deed. The qualities of nature act upon the qualities of nature, yet the ego, deluded by itself, insists upon the claim, 'I am the doer.' Krishna then explains that this false ownership is what binds a person to the results of their work.

verses.sa: तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः । गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥
verses.tr: The one who truly understands the division of qualities and actions does not cling, seeing that qualities act upon qualities.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts from action to awareness, showing the wise person how to stand apart. Listen to how he names the true actor.

body.text: The one who truly understands the division of qualities and actions does not cling, seeing that qualities act upon qualities. Krishna points to one truth, guna acting on guna. The wise person sees that the gunas are moving the gunas, and with that sight, the ego who claims to be the doer simply vanishes. Next, Krishna shows what happens when a person forgets this truth and clings to the ego of doing.

verses.sa: प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु । तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् ॥
verses.tr: The ignorant, deluded by the qualities of nature, cling to actions born of those qualities. The wise should not unsettle those who do not yet understand fully.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna tells Arjuna to listen for the word kritsnavit, the one who knows fully, and to hear what this knower is told not to do to the ignorant.

body.text: The ignorant, deluded by the qualities of nature, cling to actions born of those qualities. The wise should not unsettle those who do not yet understand fully. Krishna uses kritsnavit, the one who knows fully, to describe a wise person, and then commands them not to unsettle the dull-minded. The wise should not disturb those who do not yet understand fully. Krishna then turns to the knower's own duty, asking them to surrender all action to him and fight without attachment.

verses.sa: मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा । निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥
verses.tr: Surrender all actions to me with the disciplined mind. Free from desire, possessiveness, and sorrow, fight.
verses.angle: Surrender all actions to me with a focused mind
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna offers a path to act without inner collapse. Listen to how he tells Arjuna to surrender every action inward.

body.text: Surrender all actions to me with the disciplined mind. Free from desire, possessiveness, and sorrow, fight. Surrender every action to Krishna, drop desire and 'mine', and fight without fever, he tells Arjuna. Krishna names the exact state that must be present before the battle: free from desire, free from possessiveness, and free from distress.

verses.sa: ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः । श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ॥
verses.tr: Those who always follow this teaching of Mine with trust and without fault-finding are freed from the bonds of action.
verses.angle: anusuyantah: the inner state that breaks karma's chains
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna carries forward the promise of freedom, now naming the exact inner state required to break the chains of karma.

body.text: Those who always follow this teaching of Mine with trust and without fault-finding are freed from the bonds of action. Notice the word anusuyantah, without fault-finding. The teaching does not free the one who watches for flaws; it frees the one who simply accepts and follows. Krishna immediately warns that those who do find fault are lost, turning the teaching into a clear choice.

verses.sa: ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् । सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ॥
verses.tr: But those who, finding fault with this teaching, do not follow it, know them to be deluded in all knowledge and ruined in understanding.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Why does Krishna warn that rejecting his teaching leads to ruin? Listen to the exact state he assigns to those who refuse it.

body.text: But those who, finding fault with this teaching, do not follow it, know them to be deluded in all knowledge and ruined in understanding. The word is abhyasuyantah, finding fault. It is the closed mind that refuses to listen and instead looks for flaws, leaving the person lost in every kind of knowledge. Krishna then turns to the wise, explaining that even they act according to their own nature, making restraint impossible to force.

verses.sa: सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि । प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥
verses.tr: Even the wise act according to their own nature. All beings follow nature; what can restraint do?
verses.angle: Even the wise act from their nature
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts from blaming Arjuna to describing human nature. Listen for the single word that surprises him.

body.text: Even the wise act according to their own nature. All beings follow nature; what can restraint do? Even the wise, the ones who know the truth, still act from their own nature. Krishna admits that force and suppression cannot change this deep-rooted pattern. He then names the two forces that control the senses, attachment and aversion. He calls them your enemies. Listen to how he describes them.

verses.sa: इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ । तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥
verses.tr: Attachment and aversion sit in every sense-object. Do not come under their power, for they are your enemies on the path.
verses.angle: Paripanthinau: the two enemies on the path
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna warns Arjuna that two enemies are already waiting in every object he touches. Listen for the exact names of these two forces.

body.text: Attachment and aversion sit in every sense-object. Do not come under their power, for they are your enemies on the path. Listen for the word paripanthinau, the two enemies on the path. Attachment and aversion sit established in every sense-object, and Krishna calls them the two enemies on the path. Krishna then says that even the wise act according to their own nature, and asks where a person should focus their effort.

verses.sa: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
verses.tr: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than another's duty well performed. Better death in one's own duty; another's duty is dangerous.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna speaks to Arjuna, who is frozen between his warrior role and his fear of killing relatives. Listen for the logic Krishna uses to pull him back to his own role.

body.text: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than another's duty well performed. Better death in one's own duty; another's duty is dangerous. Listen to one word, svadharmah, one's own duty. Krishna ranks your own role, done imperfectly, above someone else's role done well. Krishna now warns Arjuna against the peril of adopting another's path, no matter how perfect it looks.
